Then a Mexican speaker opens their mouth at full conversational speed, and that preparation seems completely irrelevant. That gap isn't personal failure ; it's structural . "The disconnect between classroom Spanish and real Mexican Spanish isn't a learner problem — it's a curriculum problem. Standard courses are built around a version of the language that most native speakers simply don't use in everyday conversation." 💡 Tip: If you've completed a Spanish course and still struggle with Mexican Spanish , don't restart from scratch — targeted exposure to regional speech patterns is far more effective than repeating general lessons . ⚠️ Warning: Relying solely on textbook Spanish can create a false sense of readiness. Real conversational fluency requires exposure to the specific rhythms, slang, and speed of Mexican Spanish — not just the standardized version. Traditional courses often teach a standardised form of Spanish, while real Mexican Spanish includes regional vocabulary, faster speech, and everyday colloquialisms: Neutral/Castilian vocabulary → Regional Mexican slang and expressions – Everyday speech includes words and phrases specific to Mexico and its regions. Slow, enunciated speech → Full conversational speed – Native speakers may speak quickly, blend words, and reduce or drop sounds. Formal grammar structures → Informal contractions and colloquialisms – Real conversations frequently use shortened forms and casual expressions. Standard pronunciation → Distinct Mexican accent and intonation patterns – Mexican Spanish has pronunciation and rhythm patterns that learners may not encounter in standardised course material. Why is recognizing vocabulary in real speech so much harder? Knowing a language and processing it in real time are different skills. A learner can recognize "platicar" on a flashcard but miss it entirely in fast, flowing speech. Spoken-word recognition requires repeated exposure to actual sound in natural speech—something vocabulary drills don't build. Research on second-language listening confirms this: knowing vocabulary isn't enough if you can't identify it when it leaves someone's mouth. Why regional variation catches learners off guard According to the HelloTalk Blog , Spanish has 20 distinct national varieties, each with unique vocabulary, slang, and pronunciation. A learner who studied Castilian Spanish or a generic "Latin American" course may struggle in a Monterrey market or Mexico City kitchen, where vocabulary, rhythm, filler words, and contractions differ significantly. Within Mexico itself, linguistic research documents meaningful vocabulary differences across northern, central, and southern regions, so even "Mexican Spanish" lacks uniformity. Why do slang lists and apps fall short for real conversations? Most learners respond by downloading another app or memorizing slang lists. Slang without a grammar foundation produces fragments, not conversations; fragments don't hold up when a native speaker responds at full speed. Apps built around gamification reward consistency with the app, not progress toward actual conversation. Tools like Parrot take a different approach, using short-form video immersion rooted in comprehensible input theory so learners build listening comprehension through real native-speaker content, not controlled audio designed to be easy. What actually closes the gap You need to listen to authentic Spanish daily. The HelloTalk Blog notes that Mexico has over 130 million Spanish speakers, making it the largest Spanish-speaking country in the world. Mexican Spanish is the variety you're most likely to hear, and most general courses don't prepare you for it adequately. The solution is regular contact with the real sound, speed, and words of Mexican speech until you recognize them automatically. Why does context beat memorization for regional vocabulary? Regional vocabulary builds best through context, not memorization. When you hear "carro" used repeatedly in natural situations, your brain connects the word to meaning and situation simultaneously—a fundamentally different kind of learning than adding it to a flashcard deck. The gap between course Spanish and real Mexican Spanish closes once you treat general fluency as the foundation rather than the finish line. Once you understand what's missing from most learners' routines, the question of what to look for in an app becomes far more specific than expected. What Makes an App Effective for Learning Mexican Spanish? Learning specific vocabulary is the first step. A good app for learning Mexican Spanish needs to teach the common Spanish words that work everywhere, while also adding in the special vocabulary , expressions , and sounds of Mexico . Most apps do one or the other — not many do both well, and that gap is exactly where learners get stuck. "Most apps teach either universal Spanish or regional Mexican Spanish — rarely both — leaving learners underprepared for real-world conversations in Mexico." 💡 Tip: When evaluating a Spanish app, look for one that explicitly covers Mexican slang , regional expressions , and pronunciation patterns — not just generic Latin American Spanish. A generic Spanish app can build a broad foundation, while a Mexican Spanish app adds the regional language and cultural context needed for more authentic communication: Universal vocabulary – Both generic and Mexican Spanish apps can cover essential vocabulary shared across Spanish-speaking regions. Mexican slang & expressions – Generic apps rarely focus on regional expressions, while a Mexican Spanish app can teach the phrases learners are more likely to encounter in Mexico. Regional pronunciation – Generic apps may not target Mexico-specific pronunciation patterns, whereas a specialised app can provide dedicated regional listening and pronunciation practice. Mexico-specific cultural context – A Mexican Spanish app can incorporate cultural references and situations that make the language more relevant to everyday life in Mexico. 🎯 Key Point: The real difference between a good and great app is whether it bridges universal Spanish fluency with authentic Mexican vocabulary — because that gap is where most learners get stuck. Why vocabulary depth matters more than variety Students often collect words in isolation rather than learning them in context. A word heard during conversation, connected to a person and feeling, stays in memory better than a word on a flashcard. Worthwhile apps teach vocabulary through repetition in meaningful situations, not through drills that reward recognition without building recall. According to the App Store listing for Learn Mexican Spanish Words by PLANB LABS OU, the app offers 2,700+ words across 150+ topics available for free, supporting genuine vocabulary acquisition rather than surface-level familiarity. What native exposure actually changes Listening to native Mexican speakers is how you learn to understand Spanish . When your ear adjusts to the rhythm, dropped syllables, and regional vowel sounds, understanding becomes automatic rather than requiring mental translation. A learner who hears only textbook Spanish will struggle in real conversation, not from insufficient vocabulary, but because natural speech's speed and sound feel unfamiliar. The best apps close this gap by using real voices instead of instructors reading slowly in a studio. Why does calibrated content matter more than raw exposure? Most learners watch Mexican TV or YouTube videos hoping context fills gaps. This works eventually, but content is rarely calibrated to their level. When material is too fast or complex, understanding breaks down and engagement stops. Parrot addresses this with short-form video structured around comprehensible input: material challenging enough to stretch understanding without overwhelming it, with spaced repetition ensuring vocabulary transfers to long-term memory. The slang trap and why it misleads learners Mexican slang is not a shortcut. Learners who chase regional expressions before building a solid Spanish base end up with a party trick, not a conversation. Slang varies by age, region within Mexico, and social context. Without the grammatical and lexical foundation to read those cues, you will miss the mark. The right sequence is broad Spanish proficiency first, regional fluency second. Why do most apps fail at pronunciation and speaking practice? Pronunciation and speaking practice are where most apps fall short. They teach you to recognize sounds but not produce them. Mexican Spanish has distinct intonation patterns compared to Castilian or Caribbean Spanish, and your mouth needs repetition to approximate those sounds, not just your ears. An app that includes speaking prompts, shadowing exercises, or interaction with native speech provides the physical habit of forming sounds correctly—something passive listening alone cannot. How much does consistency matter for making progress? Consistency determines whether any of this works. Ten focused minutes daily beats two hours on a Sunday. The best apps fit into existing habits rather than demanding a restructured schedule. Once you know what to look for, the harder question is which apps deliver it. 10 Best Apps to Learn Mexican Spanish Each app solves a different problem. The real question isn't which one is best overall: it's which one closes the specific gap between you and a real conversation in Mexican Spanish. 1. Parrot — Best for Authentic Mexican Spanish Exposure Most learners start with structured lessons because they feel safe and easy to measure. The problem emerges later: when a Mexican speaker talks at normal speed, you understand almost nothing, because lessons built around controlled sentences don't train your ear for real speech. How does Parrot build real listening skills in context? Parrot uses short videos from native speakers as its main learning tool, pairing comprehensible input with spaced repetition so vocabulary stays in context rather than isolation. Learners tap unfamiliar words while watching, save them immediately, and review them through a personalized system matched to their level. The format integrates naturally into existing daily scroll habits, making consistency automatic. What should learners know before choosing Parrot? The catch: Parrot's value for Mexican Spanish depends on your feed's content—it isn't a Mexico-only curriculum. For learners who want to move beyond controlled sentences and hear how Mexican speakers actually talk, our platform fills a gap that grammar apps cannot . 2. Duolingo — Best for Building a Consistent Beginner Foundation According to makesyoufluent.com's 2025 review of the best Spanish language apps, Duolingo has over 500 million users worldwide. However, it excels at building habits rather than teaching fluency. Duolingo's game-like structure encourages daily practice, and for beginners, this regularity builds vocabulary and sentence pattern knowledge. However, Duolingo's course teaches general Spanish, not Mexican Spanish specifically. You won't find Mexican slang, regional pronunciation, or the rhythm of casual Mexico City conversation in the lessons. Use it to build a beginner foundation, then add content that sounds like the Spanish you want to speak. 3. Pimsleur — Best for Audio-Based Speaking Practice Pimsleur is built for learners who want to practice speaking while commuting, exercising, or multitasking. Its guided audio lessons focus on pronunciation and conversational recall , making it one of the stronger tools for developing spoken output without sitting at a desk. Pimsleur offers distinct Spanish courses, including a Spain-focused option. If your goal is Mexican Spanish pronunciation and vocabulary, ensure you're using the correct course variant; this oversight can misdirect your accent for months. 4. Babbel — Best for Structured Mexican Spanish Lessons Babbel distinguishes between European Spanish and Mexican Spanish at the course level. English-speaking learners can choose the Mexican Spanish track, which progresses to B1 and includes speakers from multiple Spanish-speaking countries. Regional specificity matters because the vocabulary, phrasing, and pronunciation in early lessons shape the Spanish your brain defaults to under pressure. Structured lessons are controlled environments. Babbel builds a solid Mexican Spanish foundation but cannot replicate the unpredictability of real conversation. Pair it with authentic listening content once your foundation stabilizes. 5. LingQ — Best for Learning Through Mexican Spanish Content If you've already built a foundation and want to develop reading and listening depth, LingQ gives you access to authentic Mexican Spanish material: podcasts, articles, and video transcripts. You work through content at your own pace, marking unknown words and tracking comprehension over time. The constraint is real: LingQ provides access, not curation. You must select material that matches your level and targets the Mexican Spanish variety you want. A library isn't a curriculum; the discipline to use it well must come from you. 6. italki — Best for Practicing With Mexican Tutors Speaking practice with a real person solves what no app can replicate: the pressure, spontaneity, and feedback loop of actual conversation. italki lets you search specifically for Mexican tutors, so your pronunciation feedback, vocabulary corrections, and conversational exposure match the regional variety you're targeting. Tutor selection is critical. A great Mexican tutor who adapts lessons to your goals speeds up speaking more than months of solo study. Read profiles carefully, prioritize tutors with structured lesson plans, and treat the first session as a diagnostic rather than a commitment. 7. SpanishDict — Best for Mexican Spanish Reference SpanishDict helps you find unfamiliar words, expressions, and conjugations while consuming Mexican content. It provides definitions, pronunciation, regional usage notes, and full conjugation tables, making it a useful reference layer alongside other learning methods. The limitation: looking up vocabulary builds awareness but not the automatic recall needed for real-time conversation. Reference tools support fluency; they don't create it. 8. Tandem — Best for Language Exchange With Mexican Speakers Tandem connects learners with over 42,000 native Mexican speakers on its platform, offering direct access to informal Mexican Spanish, regional expressions, and conversational rhythm that structured apps cannot provide. The main limitation is that language exchange isn't the same as instruction. Your partner isn't trained to correct grammar consistently, and conversations can drift toward being social rather than educational. Use Tandem to practice what you've already learned, not to learn things for the first time. 9. YouTube — Best Free Source of Mexican Spanish Content Mexican creators on YouTube—journalists, comedians, chefs, educators—produce vast amounts of content covering speech from formal to deeply casual. That variety builds listening skills in ways most language apps cannot. The drawback is how it's set up: YouTube doesn't organize content by skill level or learning goals. You must build your own curriculum by finding Mexican creators whose speech speed and vocabulary match your current level. Start with content that's somewhat challenging but mostly understandable, and avoid fast-paced drama before your ear is ready. 10. Netflix — Best for Immersive Mexican Spanish Listening Mexican shows on Netflix like "La Casa de las Flores," "Monarca," and "Control Z" offer authentic Mexican Spanish in cultural context. Watching with Spanish audio and Spanish subtitles helps your brain connect sound, meaning, and context simultaneously, bringing you closer to real fluency than multiple-choice exercises. Netflix works best once you have a listening foundation. Use it as a reward and training tool when your comprehension is strong enough to catch at least 60 to 70 percent of what you hear without subtitles. No Single App Teaches Every Part of Mexican Spanish Each tool solves a specific problem and creates a gap: Babbel builds regional structure but can't replicate spontaneous conversation. Duolingo builds habits but lacks regional depth. italki builds speaking confidence but requires prior knowledge to draw from. YouTube and Netflix build listening fluency only for learners past the beginner stage. Which combination of tools closes your weaknesses fastest? The strongest learners treat these tools as a stack: a structured course builds the foundation, authentic content trains the ear, a tutor develops the speaking reflex, and reference tools fill gaps. The question isn't which app wins, but which combination closes your specific weaknesses fastest. Knowing the tools is only half the answer. The harder part is figuring out which one to start with. What do absolute beginners need to focus on first? People starting to learn Spanish need high-frequency vocabulary , basic sentence patterns, and correct pronunciation before learning slang or regional expressions. Trying to learn Mexican idioms before you can make simple sentences is like reading a novel before knowing the alphabet. Build your foundation first, then work on sounding authentic. Once you have a solid foundation, listening to real Mexican speech becomes comprehensible. Why do intermediate learners hit a wall with natural Mexican speech? Intermediate learners face a different problem: they can read and answer rehearsed questions, but native speech at natural speed causes comprehension to drop sharply. The issue isn't vocabulary size—it's that app-based learning rarely exposes learners to the rhythm, dropped syllables, and regional cadence of actual Mexican speech. More beginner-style lessons won't close this gap; authentic listening will. Most learners keep reaching for structured courses when they need unscripted exposure to multiple Mexican voices. What do travelers actually need when phrasebook apps fall short? Travelers often download phrasebook apps to memorize greetings, food vocabulary, and directions. This works for predictable exchanges but fails when a waiter responds off-script or a local gives directions using landmarks instead of street names. Practical communication requires flexible vocabulary to handle unexpected conversation turns. Parrot addresses this by using short-form video clips from real Mexican speakers calibrated to your comprehension level, so you absorb language as people actually speak it, not as textbooks imagine it. Does your reason for learning change what you need? People moving to Mexico and heritage learners often want to learn both the language and culture. Understanding what someone says differs from understanding why it sounds that way, what cultural references mean, or why a phrase feels warm in one situation and sharp in another. Heritage learners especially benefit from content that shows the variety of Spanish their family speaks, not a sanitized version without regional specificity. Does the type of learner you are change which tool fits best? No single app solves every problem for every type of learner. Professionals who need Mexican Spanish for client meetings require general conversation skills , industry vocabulary, and real-time confidence. Casual learners need something they'll want to use tomorrow. Consistency over months matters more than any single feature: an app with a hundred lessons you abandon after two weeks helps less than a simpler tool you use daily. Why don't general Spanish lessons provide enough authentic Mexican speech? A learner can build a strong foundation through structured lessons and still struggle to understand Mexican speakers. title: How to Build a Payroll Policy in Nigeria: A Practical Guide for Employers
summary: Business Center How to Build a Payroll Policy in Nigeria: A Practical Guide for Employers Oluwakemi Adesina August 18, 2026 When setting up a clear payroll policy in Nigeria, you need clear rules on everything from tax laws to staff complaints before anyone gets paid. Relying on inconsistent payroll procedures causes problems quickly: You calculate allowances differently every month, and employees notice. You guess your payment timelines, miss tax deadlines, and get hit with heavy fines. You don’t lock down your data, private salaries leak, and team trust is ruined. This guide changes that. It is a simple map to help you build an accurate system that keeps your HR and finance teams on the exact same page. What Is a Payroll Policy? A company payroll policy is your business playbook for employee pay. It sets the rules for when people get paid, how bonuses are paid, which taxes you must legally deduct, and how you protect private staff data. Do not confuse a policy with a procedure. Your payroll management policy sets the big ground rules, while your monthly procedures are the specific technical steps your team takes to run the numbers. Your HR and finance leaders must build this together. HR makes sure the rules are fair and match local labor habits, while finance ensures the final bill fits your budget and banking limits. What Should a Payroll Policy Include? To build a practical payroll policy template that Nigerian business managers can actually use every month, your document must clearly cover these seven areas: Payday schedule: Pick the exact day your team gets paid (like the 25th of the month). Payroll cut-off dates: Set a hard monthly deadline (like the 18th) to stop taking new overtime logs or expense claims for that cycle. New hire data rules: List what documents a new hire must submit (like their bank details and TIN) before they can join the pay run. Allowances and bonuses: Be clear about how you handle transport, housing, or 13th-month bonuses. Overtime guidelines: Define who qualifies for extra hours and exactly how those rates are calculated. Deductions: List everything that comes out of a paycheck, from government taxes to staff loan repayments. Error fixes: Give your employees a clear, calm way to flag and fix salary mistakes, just in case it happens. Setting Payroll Roles and Approval Controls Depending on your business size, one person should not handle the entire pay run, while a shared password can compromise your payroll system. If the same person types the numbers and sends the payment, you risk mistakes, and when several people have access, it’s difficult to know who changed a salary, who added an employee, or who approved a payment. Your policy must divide this work into three steps: Step 1: Preparation (HR Admin) Gathers the raw data, logs the overtime hours, and updates new onboarding profiles. Step 2: Review (Finance Manager) Double-checks the calculations, confirms tax tiers, and cross-references the master budget. Step 3: Approval (CFO/Founder): Approves and locks down the monthly run. Protect your business by using strict role-based access in your software to build solid payroll controls. Eazipay has a feature called roles and permissions that gives access to one owner who eventually brings the right team as part of the payroll work and every process update is documented clearly. HR staff should only edit basic employee details and involve the right HR associates, while accountants handle financial fields and involve the right financial associates when required. Locking these permissions prevents unauthorized changes, keeps responsibility clear as the business grows and ensures nothing is modified without passing through the official payroll approval process. Managing Statutory and Other Payroll Deductions Mistakes in remittances lead to penalties in Nigeria. Your policy must outline exact calculation rules and monthly deadlines to follow: Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) Tax: You must deduct personal income tax from your staff and pay it to the State Internal Revenue Service where they live. These tax rates must follow the official rules set by the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS). Pension Contributions: Under the Pension Reform Act, you must run a mandatory monthly split, usually 10% from the employer and 8% from the employee. These funds must go to registered Pension Fund Administrators following the rules managed by the National Pension Commission (PenCom). National Housing Fund (NHF): If your team qualifies, a specific percentage of their basic salary must be deducted and paid monthly toward federal housing plans, following the framework run by the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN). Beyond these laws, your policy should set clear caps on other deductions like salary advances so employees always take home a fair wage. Handling Payroll Errors, Corrections and Employee Disputes Even with good software, mistakes happen. An allowance may be missed or a tax rate miscalculated if not properly documented. When an employee spots an issue on their payslip, they need to know how to get it fixed calmly. Your salary payment policy should follow a simple, fast timeline: Flag it: The employee emails HR within 5 days of payday. Check it: The payroll admin checks the records and confirms the error. Fix it: If they were underpaid, you send a supplementary transfer within 48 hours, or add it to the next month if they prefer. Every single fix must create a clear digital audit trail so your books stay totally clean. Payroll Data, Records and Confidentiality Your payroll records hold sensitive information; bank accounts, home addresses, and base salaries. If this data leaks, it harms office morale and violates privacy standards. Include these rules in your policy: Only designated HR and finance leaders get access to master payroll files. Make strong passwords and multi-factor authentication (MFA) mandatory on all accounting software. title: Best SUV Lease Deals in August 2026
summary: Discover the best SUV lease deals available this month, and learn about the benefits and drawbacks of leasing an SUV versus other forms of ownership.
body_text: SUVs have been incredibly popular for well over a decade. And their combination of utility and all-wheel drive (AWD) or four-wheel drive (4WD) capability shows no signs of losing its appeal. In fact, data from IHS Markit suggests these days almost half of all the new vehicles sold in the United States are SUVs. Some brands, like Buick and Lincoln, even sell SUVs exclusively. Now consider that leasing is a popular form of vehicle ownership, and it will make sense that there is an explosion in interest from people looking to get the best possible leasing deals on new SUVs. We’ve created this guide of lease deals that we update regularly to make the lease research process as easy as possible. Below, you’ll find the best SUV lease deals this month, whether you’re looking at a compact midsize SUV, or full-size luxury SUV, or even an electric vehicle. You’ll also find tips and advice on how to get the best price and secure the deal that makes the most sense for you. The Best SUV Lease Deals in August 2026 Benefits of Leasing an SUV Drawbacks of Leasing an SUV SUV Lease Trends in 2026 The Best SUV Lease Deals this Month How to Get the Best SUV Lease Offers Leasing Used SUVs Benefits of Leasing an SUV The most significant incentive for most people to lease an SUV as opposed to finance deals or other purchase methods is keeping a lower monthly payment . This is because the lease amount covers only the depreciation of the SUV over the term of the lease. A purchase means you’re paying the entire value of the SUV. Leasing also creates flexibility for people who like to upgrade their vehicle and/or drive a new vehicle most of the time. A lease usually lasts two to four years, so if you love to be in the hottest BMW or Mercedes-Benz and aren’t worried about actually owning it, a lease may be a good fit for you. Lease deals typically focus on new cars rather than used cars, so another lease benefit is driving a car with lower costs of ownership and repairs, along with the latest design, safety, and tech features. With some SUVs like Toyotas or Chevrolets, the off-roading features are the most modern available. And new cars tend to be more fuel efficient than their predecessors as well. Of course, having a warranty on your leased new car is attractive. Like specials offered with car buying, there are usually lease specials and rebates to be had, too. Drawbacks of Leasing an SUV First off, you don’t actually own a vehicle when you lease it. This means you don’t have your SUV to show for all those monthly payments at the end of the lease term. Lease agreements also have mileage limits, and if you go over them you’ll have to pay extra money at the end of the lease term. Be aware, too, that you must keep your leased SUV in tip-top shape. Just like extra miles, any excessive wear and tear can lead to extra fees at the end of the term. And it feels pretty crummy to give that SUV back to the dealership and pay a lot of money when you do it. If any of these drawbacks give you pause, you may want to reconsider whether car leasing is a good idea. SUV Lease Trends in 2026 The new car market continues to rebound from the pandemic, and though there were impacts due to chip shortages, rising inflation and interest rates, the market is improving. That said, lessees may still find it difficult to find the specific SUV they want, and there may be fewer deals than pre-pandemic. This is true for most manufacturers, from Honda to Cadillac. The good news is that there are still lease deals to be had, whether you’re shopping for a full-size three-row SUV or a subcompact SUV or anything in between. There are incentives on all types of SUVs and we’ve selected the ones we rate as the best SUV lease deals around right now. More good news is that there are opportunities to score good leases on both mass-market SUVs and luxury SUV models. Interestingly, dealers are extending lease terms for longer amounts of time, making for more attractive monthly lease payments for lessees. Note that deals may differ by location and are subject to withdrawal. Consult your local dealer for the best lease offers nearby. Research the Kia Sportage Plug-in Hybrid on CarGurus How to Get the Best SUV Lease Offers Just like looking for the best car deals when buying, finding the best lease deals means shopping around. It doesn’t matter if you’re in the market for a crossover, SUV, a truck or a sedan, it pays to do your homework. This also means understanding the language of auto finance. It sounds intimidating, but once you know the difference between the MSRP (the car’s list price, often printed on the window sticker, also the amount of money paid when financing), and the net cap cost (the price you negotiate with the dealer, including incentives, the amount of money paid for a lease), you’ll understand how your monthly lease payment is determined. Be on the lookout for rebates, especially if you’re interested in an electric SUV. Ask if there is accessibility to state tax credits to apply to your EV lease. For more details on leasing terminology, see our guide: What you need to know when getting a car loan . Research Available Financing Options It’s a good idea to investigate other forms of purchasing a vehicle, especially if you think you’re going to wind up buying the car at the end of the lease term. These options include secured auto loans, bank loans and of course dealership loans. You will most likely wind up finding that the monthly costs with car buying are higher than with the lease, because you’re paying for the entire cost of the car and not just a portion of the depreciation. But be sure you know what kinds of specials are out there, and ask if there are any specials or car buying incentives to be had. If you are concerned about how your credit score could affect your ability to lease a car, see our guide to buying a car with bad credit . Leverage Trade-Ins and Additional Incentives There are several levers that can be pulled when negotiating an SUV lease deal. First is the price you’ve negotiated with the dealer, also known as the net cap cost. Another lever is your down payment. It’s not always a great idea to put a bunch of money down on a lease, so see what kind of wiggle room you have. The interest rate, duration of the lease term, and the mileage limits may all be negotiable. Don’t be afraid to ask for a better arrangement that will be more suitable for you. For example, If the monthly cost of an SUV lease deal isn’t quite as affordable as you need, the dealer might be able (and willing) to adjust one of these factors to bring that monthly lease payment more in line with your budget. Also, don’t forget that a trade-in can be a great way to get a good monthly payment arranged, but also don’t forget to compare the dealer’s offer with other dealers or the price you’d get selling it on your own. Getting a free offer via CarGurus Sell My Car service is a great place to start. Leasing Used SUVs Yes, it is possible to lease a used SUV but it’s not easy to find a dealership who will do one. You’ll need to do some legwork. That said, even though few dealerships offer this arrangement, it can be the most affordable way to get into a new SUV. Again, the lease is determined on the amount of depreciation on the vehicle. By the time the vehicle is a few years old, it’s taken the largest hit on that depreciation. Bear in mind that this may be the most difficult time to track down a used SUV to lease, as there just isn’t as much inventory out there. But it doesn’t mean it’s not worth looking around to see what you can find. Know that some of the benefits of leasing a new car may not apply to this scenario. For example, a full warranty may not be available, and the vehicle may not be as reliable since it has some wear and tear on it. There may not be any specials or incentives. But the monthly payment on a used vehicle will be pretty low without them. If you can pin down an SUV to lease, know that you may be getting one of the best SUV lease deals around. title: Newell Brands Announces Upsizing and Pricing of $600 Million 6.250% Senior Notes due 2031
summary: ATLANTA --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 5, 2026-- Newell Brands (NASDAQ: NWL) today announced the upsizing and pricing of $600 million aggregate principal amount of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due 2031 (the “Notes”) in an offering (the “Offering”) that is exempt from the registration requirements of the
body_text: PDF Version ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 5, 2026-- Newell Brands (NASDAQ: NWL) today announced the upsizing and pricing of $600 million aggregate principal amount of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due 2031 (the “Notes”) in an offering (the “Offering”) that is exempt from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). The offering of the Notes is expected to close on August 19, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Newell Brands intends to use the net proceeds from the sale of the Notes in the Offering to redeem in full its outstanding 6.375% senior notes due 2027 (the “2027 Notes”), pay related fees and expenses in connection with the Offering and the redemption, and repay a portion of the amount outstanding under its five-year asset-based revolving credit facility, dated as of July 30, 2026. Neither this press release nor anything contained herein shall constitute a notice of redemption or an offer to redeem or purchase any of the outstanding 2027 Notes. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any securities. The Notes are being offered only to qualified institutional buyers in reliance on the exemption from registration set forth in Rule 144A under the Securities Act, and outside the United States to certain non-U.S. persons in reliance on the exemption from registration set forth in Regulation S under the Securities Act. The Notes have not been registered under the Securities Act, or the securities laws of any state or other jurisdiction, and may not be offered or sold in the United States without registration or an applicable exemption from the Securities Act and applicable state securities or blue sky laws and foreign securities laws. About Newell Brands Newell Brands (NASDAQ: NWL) is a leading global consumer goods company with a strong portfolio of well-known brands, including Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Graco, Coleman, Rubbermaid Commercial Products, Yankee Candle, Paper Mate, FoodSaver, Dymo, EXPO, Elmer’s, Oster, NUK, Spontex and Campingaz. Newell Brands is focused on delighting consumers by lighting up everyday moments. title: AVAX One Announces Financial Leadership Change
body_text: WEST PALM BEACH, FL, Aug. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — AVAX One Technology Ltd. (Nasdaq: AVX) (“AVAX One” or the “Company”), today announced the departure of Chief Financial Officer (“CFO”) Chris Polimeni, effective August 17, 2026. Stephanie Brady, the Company’s Controller, has been promoted to Chief Accounting Officer and will oversee the Company’s financial reporting function.

title: LlamaLab vs ChartRequest vs Codes Health
summary: Compare LlamaLab, ChartRequest, and Codes Health for plaintiff medical record retrieval. See how Codes Health pairs complete records in a couple of weeks with human-verified AI analysis and flat fee pricing.
body_text: When plaintiff law firms evaluate medical record retrieval solutions, the choice between LlamaLab, ChartRequest, and Codes Health comes down to one question: do you want records fast, or do you want complete, litigation-ready documentation with AI-powered case analysis attached? Same-day retrieval sounds great until gaps surface later and turn into follow-up cycles, client frustration, and holes in your evidence. Codes Health is built for plaintiff attorneys who want complete, verified records in a couple of weeks with AI analysis that turns thousands of pages into usable case insights. Key Takeaways Codes Health differentiates itself by combining record retrieval with human-verified, litigation-focused analysis, including Missing Record Review, breach-of-care indicators, and future medical expense extraction Same-day digital retrieval can be limited to records available through connected sources, so firms should verify that every requested provider, date range, and record type has been covered. Missing records may require further client involvement and can contribute to dissatisfaction or churn General AI tools are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review, and Codes Health's purpose-built platform delivers human-verified insights built for plaintiff cases ChartRequest concentrates on retrieval infrastructure serving both healthcare and legal requestors, so firms wanting chronologies or case analysis typically source those separately LlamaLab is a defendant in an Epic Systems lawsuit filed on January 13, 2026. The allegations remain disputed, and LlamaLab has moved to dismiss the claims Codes Health's Filevine integration removes platform switching by embedding retrieval into case files, with custom integrations available for high-volume clients on other CRM platforms 1. Codes Health: Integrated Retrieval and Analysis for Plaintiff Firms Codes Health is purpose-built for plaintiff litigation, pairing comprehensive retrieval with AI-powered case analysis reviewed by medical and legal specialists. Founded in 2024 by MIT and Yale graduates, the company is backed by institutional investors including Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Amplify Partners, and Haystack. What Sets Codes Health Apart: Missing Record Review : Proactively identifies documentation gaps by cross-referencing patient history before records reach your legal team, heading off trial surprises Breach-of-Care Indicators : AI flags potential standard-of-care deviations that matter for medical malpractice work Human-Reviewed AI Analysis : All AI-generated insights are reviewed by humans before delivery, reducing the risk of hallucinations and material errors Future Medical Expense Extraction : Pulls documented future expenses out of the records for damage calculations Pre-Existing Condition Flagging : Surfaces prior injuries and conditions that shape case strategy Retrieval Capabilities: Codes Health retrieves medical, billing, and imaging records through multiple channels: Claims clearinghouses Custodian integrations Proprietary provider networks Patient portals Traditional fax, email, and telephone follow-up Patient upload workflows Completeness-First Philosophy: Rather than racing to deliver same-day results, Codes Health prioritizes complete, litigation-ready documentation in a couple of weeks. In practice, that means: Records verified against the original request before delivery Gaps identified and resolved proactively Fewer follow-up cycles pull your client back into the process Documentation is ready for case development from the start Flat Fee Pricing: Codes Health uses flat fee pricing rather than per-page pricing, covering retrieval, AI chronologies, breach-of-care indicators, Missing Record Review, and human review. Firms should confirm contract terms for custodian fees, certifications, and re-requests. Integration Capabilities: The Filevine partnership embeds medical record retrieval directly into case files. Legal teams can request, track, communicate, and receive records without leaving their case management system. For high-volume firms on other platforms, Codes Health builds custom integrations with CRM systems and medical software. Continuous Platform Evolution: Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, ensuring the platform constantly evolves, improves, and becomes more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. Best For: Personal injury firms that need complete documentation Medical malpractice practices need breach-of-care analysis Mass tort firms are processing high case volumes Workers' compensation and disability practices Any plaintiff firm using Filevine 2. LlamaLab: Speed-First Retrieval LlamaLab, founded in 2024 and headquartered in New York, markets same-day medical record retrieval for plaintiff law firms. The platform serves plaintiff firms nationwide and emphasizes rapid turnaround for case screening. LlamaLab Features: Same-day to 48-hour retrieval for electronically connected providers, with alternative retrieval methods for sources without direct access Provider discovery identifying treatment locations Clinical qualification team for case screening Litify integration that returns completed work and status updates to the matter AI summaries, timelines, chronologies, search, case analytics, and AI chat Key Considerations: Completeness Verification : Same-day digital retrieval can be limited to records available through connected sources. LlamaLab notes that delivery depends on the provider. Firms should verify that every requested provider, date range, and record type has been covered, since missing records may require further client involvement and can contribute to dissatisfaction or churn. Pending Litigation : LlamaLab is a defendant in an Epic Systems lawsuit filed on January 13, 2026, concerning record access methods. The allegations remain disputed, and LlamaLab has moved to dismiss the claims. Firms with heightened compliance review processes may want to track the docket. Analysis Capabilities : LlamaLab advertises clinical intelligence, AI summaries, timelines, chronologies, and case analytics. Firms comparing it with Codes Health should look at how each platform handles breach-of-care indicators and completeness verification before delivery. Pricing Structure : As of August 4, 2026, LlamaLab publishes a Basic plan at $50 per medical record request, $50 per billing record request, a $150 case setup fee, and 12 cents per uploaded page. Its Core Unlimited plan advertises unlimited medical and billing requests with 1,000 uploaded pages included and 10 cents per additional page, with the plan price available by quote. Both plans include their AI analysis platform. Best For: Firms that want a fast turnaround for early case screening Mass tort intake requiring rapid qualification decisions Practices using Litify case management 3. ChartRequest (CaseBinder): Retrieval-First Platform ChartRequest, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Atlanta, operates an electronic health information platform serving healthcare providers, researchers, patients, and legal requestors. Its CaseBinder product is the legal-facing workflow. ChartRequest Features: Network of more than 10,000 healthcare organizations Real-time request tracking Authorization center and eAuthorization workflows for release management Dedicated retrieval coordinator support Digital notary services Built-in DICOM imaging viewer Per-request pricing model, with a current 90-day promotion at $35 per request and no setup fee Key Considerations: Retrieval Focus : ChartRequest concentrates on retrieval rather than AI-powered chronologies, case summaries, or legal insights. Firms wanting that layer typically organize records internally or bring in a separate chronology provider, which adds cost and paralegal time. Dual-Market Design : The platform serves healthcare provider workflows alongside legal requestors, so its emphasis differs from tools designed exclusively around plaintiff case preparation. Per-Request Pricing : ChartRequest charges per request, with provider fees passed through separately. In cases involving several providers, those costs add up. Average Turnaround : ChartRequest reports an average CaseBinder turnaround of roughly 14 days. Best For: Firms with variable case volume that want per-request flexibility Practices needing digital notary services Teams working across healthcare-oriented workflows Understanding the Medical Records Retrieval Landscape The retrieval market has changed a lot, with AI-powered platforms reshaping what used to be an entirely manual process. For plaintiff firms, the right pick is the difference between efficient case preparation and months of chasing paper. The Evolution of Medical Record Management: Traditional retrieval built on phone calls, faxes, and manual follow-up can stretch weeks or months and eat significant paralegal time. Modern platforms connect through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, and proprietary provider networks to speed that up. Speed alone does not solve the underlying problem of whether records are complete and organized for litigation. This is where general-purpose AI tools come up short. Platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. They lack the specialized training, verification layer, and legal context case preparation requires, and their outputs need qualified review before anyone relies on them. Key Features to Evaluate: Completeness verification : Does the platform check delivered records against the original request? AI analysis depth : Are chronologies litigation-grade, with human review? Breach-of-care indicators : Important for medical malpractice cases Integration capabilities : Does it work inside your case management system? Pricing transparency : Flat fees versus per-request or per-provider models Protected health information handling : Security controls and appropriate agreements The Role of Release of Information in Record Retrieval Release of Information forms are the legal gateway to medical records, and incomplete or incorrect authorizations are among the most common causes of retrieval delays and rejections. Common ROI Challenges: Missing patient signatures Incomplete date ranges Provider-specific form requirements Expired authorizations Incorrect facility information Preventing Authorization Errors: Codes Health identifies incomplete or defective authorizations as a leading cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force a rejection and resubmission, restarting the applicable deadline. Under HIPAA's individual right-of-access rule, a covered entity generally has 30 calendar days to act, subject to a permitted extension, though shorter periods apply where state law or the request type establishes one. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. Streamlining Authorization Processes: AI-assisted validation that checks authorizations before submission HIPAA-compliant e-signature workflows for intake documents Provider-specific requirement checking to prevent rejections Proactive error prevention that reduces delays from the start That pre-submission validation catches incomplete authorization forms, missing dates, incorrect provider information, and absent signatures that would otherwise cost weeks. Evaluating Speed and Efficiency in Medical Record Requests The tension between speed and completeness defines this market, and understanding the trade-off helps firms choose well. The Trade-Off With Same-Day Retrieval: Fast turnaround is genuinely useful, but it can come with downstream costs: Partial documentation that requires follow-up requests Client involvement to track down what did not arrive Multiple retrieval cycles that extend the real case timeline Staff time spent chasing records that should have been complete Completeness Over Speed: The Codes Health approach, delivering complete records in a couple of weeks rather than partial records in hours, is designed to speed up case preparation overall by: Cutting down re-request cycles Reducing client touchpoints Providing documentation ready for case development from the start Including AI analysis that would otherwise take weeks of paralegal time Real-Time Visibility: Whatever platform you use, your team needs visibility into retrieval status. Codes Health provides status information and communication directly inside Filevine case files, so nobody is logging into a separate portal or emailing for an update. Handling Protected Health Information Medical record platforms handle protected health information, and the obligations that attach depend on the parties' legal roles. A Business Associate Agreement is required when a vendor acts as a business associate of a covered entity or another business associate, not automatically whenever an organization touches PHI. Security Considerations to Evaluate: Business Associate Agreements where the relationship calls for one SOC 2 Type 2 certification as evidence of ongoing security controls Encryption standards , such as TLS 1.2 or higher in transit and AES-256 at rest Access controls , including role-based permissions and audit logging Codes Health operates as a HIPAA-compliant platform and documents AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, role-based access controls, audit trails, and BAAs with relevant vendors. That coverage extends across retrieval, processing, analysis, and storage. The Filevine Integration: Embedded Case Management Workflow In July 2026, Filevine announced a strategic partnership with Codes Health that goes beyond a standard third-party integration. The partnership embeds medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine legal case-management environment. Benefits of Embedded Workflows: Submit requests directly from the relevant case file Validate authorizations with AI checking before submission Track progress in real time within the case project Communicate with the Codes Health team without leaving Filevine Receive completed records delivered back into the appropriate project Review history and completeness status from one place Filevine CEO Ryan Anderson described medical record retrieval as a long-standing customer pain point that customers had been asking the company to solve for years. Custom Integrations for Other Platforms: For high-volume firms on other case management systems, Codes Health builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and medical software, so the workflow benefits reach beyond the Filevine ecosystem. Comparing AI Capabilities: Insights Extraction and Summarization AI capabilities across these platforms vary widely, and understanding the differences helps firms judge real value. Beyond Basic Summaries: General AI tools can generate summaries, but litigation asks for more precision: Diagnosis identification with ICD code correlation Treatment pattern analysis for damage documentation Gap detection, identifying missing appointments or records Pre-existing condition flagging for case strategy Future expense extraction from documented medical needs The Human Review Difference: Codes Health combines AI processing with human expert review, which the company describes as AI insights verified by humans . That hybrid approach: Reduces the risk of AI hallucinations reaching legal teams Supports confidence in materials headed toward trial Addresses reliability concerns inherent in pure AI output Pairs the speed of automation with expert review Why General AI Falls Short: General-purpose AI can summarize and help you understand medical information, but it is not built for litigation-grade review because it: Lacks specialized medical-legal training Cannot verify findings against the underlying documentation Misses context that matters for case evaluation Can produce plausible-sounding conclusions that need a qualified review Codes Health's purpose-built AI platform, built specifically for plaintiff litigation, is designed for the precision case preparation and trial work demands. Making the Right Choice for Your Firm Choose Codes Health When You Need: Complete, litigation-ready records in a couple of weeks AI-powered chronologies with human review Breach-of-care indicators for medical malpractice cases Missing Record Review that surfaces gaps early Flat fee pricing for predictable costs Filevine integration or custom CRM connectivity Consider LlamaLab When: Fast initial screening is your priority Your firm uses Litify case management You have staff capacity to verify coverage and follow up where needed Consider ChartRequest When: You want per-request pricing flexibility Digital notary services are required Your practice spans healthcare-oriented workflows The Bottom Line for Plaintiff Firms All three platforms are credible, and the right one depends on where your firm actually loses time. LlamaLab leads on speed for connected providers and packages AI analysis with retrieval. ChartRequest brings a long-established retrieval network with coordinator support and per-request flexibility. Codes Health is built around plaintiff work end-to-end, pairing retrieval with pre-submission authorization validation, persistent provider follow-up, Missing Record Review, and human-reviewed litigation analysis inside your case file. If the recurring headache at your firm is records that arrive fast but are incomplete, or chronology work that has to be sourced separately, the combination of complete records in a couple of weeks, human review, and flat fee pricing is what changes the math across a caseload. Schedule a demonstration to see how Codes Health handles your firm's medical records workflow. Frequently Asked Questions What is the main difference between LlamaLab, ChartRequest, and Codes Health for medical record retrieval? The difference is in how retrieval and analysis fit together. Codes Health combines complete medical record retrieval with litigation-focused AI analysis, including breach-of-care indicators, future expense extraction, and Missing Record Review, all reviewed by humans before delivery. LlamaLab emphasizes same-day speed for electronically connected providers and includes its own AI analysis platform. ChartRequest concentrates on retrieval infrastructure, so chronologies and case organization typically come from elsewhere. How does Codes Health handle protected health information? Codes Health operates as a HIPAA-compliant platform and documents encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access controls, audit trails, and Business Associate Agreements with relevant vendors. That coverage runs across retrieval, processing, AI analysis, and storage. Can Codes Health integrate with existing legal case management software like Filevine? Yes. Codes Health has an embedded Filevine integration that lets legal teams request, track, communicate, and receive records entirely within Filevine case files. For high-volume firms on other platforms, Codes Health builds custom integrations with CRM systems and medical software. What types of legal practices benefit most from using Codes Health's platform? Codes Health serves seven legal practice areas: personal injury, mass torts, medical malpractice, workers' compensation, disability law, insurance litigation, and wrongful death. Medical malpractice practices benefit particularly from breach-of-care indicators, while personal injury and mass tort firms gain efficiency from AI-powered chronologies and Missing Record Review. Why can same-day retrieval produce incomplete records? Same-day retrieval generally depends on electronic connections to connected data sources and provider portals. That enables fast access to some records, but not every provider is electronically connected, and connected systems may not hold a complete patient history. Firms should confirm that every requested provider, date range, and record type has actually been covered, since gaps may require additional client involvement and further retrieval cycles.

title: Morningstar Investment Conference South Africa Returns with Practical Insights for a Changing World
summary: Leading industry voices explore markets, cybersecurity, evolving client expectations, practice growth and the investment implications of AI Cape Town, South Africa - Morningstar South Africa is pleased to announce the return of the Morningstar Investment Conference South Africa (MICSA) in 2026, South Africa’s largest gathering of financial advisers, taking place in Johannesburg (8 September) and Cape Town (10 September). Now in its 14 th year, the MICSA will bring together wealth and investment
body_text: Media Hotline: +1 312 696-6037 newsroom@morningstar.com View All News Morningstar Investment Conference South Africa Returns with Practical Insights for a Changing World August 13, 2026 Leading industry voices explore markets, cybersecurity, evolving client expectations, practice growth and the investment implications of AI Cape Town, South Africa - Morningstar South Africa is pleased to announce the return of the Morningstar Investment Conference South Africa (MICSA) in 2026, South Africa’s largest gathering of financial advisers, taking place in Johannesburg (8 September) and Cape Town (10 September). Now in its 14th year, the MICSA will bring together wealth and investment professionals for a full day of independent insights, practical guidance and local and global perspectives. Under the theme, “Focus on What Matters”, the conference will help advisers cut through complexity and concentrate on the insights, decisions and actions that can make the greatest difference to their practice and clients. The 2026 agenda will address cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, changing client expectations, sustainable practice growth and South Africa’s economic outlook. “At Morningstar, we remain committed to helping investors and advisers make better decisions through independent research and practical, forward-looking insights,” says Tal Nieburg, Managing Director for Morningstar South Africa. “The MICSA 2026 will give delegates clear perspectives on the changes shaping their practices and actionable ideas they can apply to deliver stronger client outcomes.” Key sessions at the MICSA 2026 include: Global Realities, Local Opportunity: mapping South Africa's road ahead Nicky Weimar, Chief Economist at Nedbank, will open the conference with a wide-angle view of the forces shaping South Africa’s economic trajectory, and, by extension, the environment clients are investing in. Expect a frank read on where momentum is genuine, where it is fragile, and where the binding constraints on growth still sit. Cybersecurity: Why Your Practice Could Make the Ideal Target Kevin Hogan, Head of Fraud & Risk at Investec Bank, and Abigail Wilson, Portfolio Specialist at Morningstar, will explain why financial advice practices are attractive targets for fraud. Advisers will gain practical guidance on strengthening processes, protecting client information and responding to an incident. The Evolving Value of Advice: What Clients Look for When They Hire a Financial Adviser Dr Ryan Murphy, Global Head of Behavioural Insights at Morningstar, will explore the emotional reasons clients choose an adviser and share practical ways to sharpen a practice’s value proposition. Navigating Global Markets How much does the location of your fund manager matter? Sean Neethling, Head of Investments South Africa, and Michael Dodd, Director: Manager Selection Services, both Morningstar, will be joined by leaders from M&G Investments, Ninety One, and PSG Asset Management to give their distinct perspectives on what it takes to build robust portfolios that are diversified across asset classes and geographies, and what actually drives client outcomes. Grow Your Own Way: Practice Success Stories Roné Swanepoel, Head of Distribution at Morningstar, will be joined by leaders from Chartered Wealth Solutions, Jurgens Group, Resolute Wealth Management and Wealth Associates to share how they have grown their businesses while maintaining strong client service and outcomes. The panel will explore the challenges they faced and lessons learned. AI in 2026: Winners, Losers and Investment Strategies Kenneth Lamont, Principal, Manager Research at Morningstar, will examine how artificial intelligence is reshaping industries and investment markets, identify potential winners and losers, and discuss approaches to AI-related opportunities. The programme will also explore global portfolio construction, South Africa’s political outlook and practical lessons in rebuilding and scaling a differentiated business. Together, these sessions will bring a focus on what matters, helping advisers to look beyond the noise and shape stronger practices and better client outcomes. Event details Johannesburg — 8 September 2026 Sandton Convention Centre [Register here] Cape Town — 10 September 2026 Cape Town International Convention Centre [Register here] Click here to view the full agenda and speaker line-up or visit the official conference website. The MICSA 2026 day programme has been accredited for 5.0 CPD points . For enquiries, please contact Conference.SouthAfrica@morningstar.com . (“the company”), a leading provider of independent investment insights in North America, Europe, Australia, Asia, and Africa. The Company offers an extensive line of products and solutions that serve a wide range of market participants, including individual and institutional investors in public and private capital markets, financial advisors and wealth managers, asset managers, retirement plan providers and sponsors, and issuers of fixed-income securities. Morningstar provides data and research insights on a wide range of investment offerings, including managed investment products, publicly listed companies, private capital markets, debt securities, and real-time global market data. Morningstar also offers investment management services through its investment advisory subsidiaries, with approximately $375 billion in assets under management and advisement as of June 30, 2026. title: AeroFlexx Partners with PLAFILM to Expand Liquid Packaging in Central America
summary: AeroFlexx and PLAFILM join forces to bring next-generation sustainable liquid packaging to brand owners across Colombia, Venezuela, and Central America, accelerating paths to commercial launch.
body_text: WEST CHESTER, Ohio, Aug. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AeroFlexx , an industry leader in sustainable liquid packaging, has announced a comprehensive partnership with Plastic Films Internacional SA (PLAFILM) to expand the commercial adoption of the AeroFlexx liquid packaging technology across Colombia, Venezuela, and the rest of Central America. The partnership combines AeroFlexx’s differentiated packaging platform with PLAFILM’s regional market knowledge and established relationships with multinationals. Together, the companies will focus on identifying applications where AeroFlexx can create measurable value across consumer experience, sustainability, supply chain performance and total system economics. The objective is to help qualified customers move efficiently from initial evaluation to commercial product launches. “Brand owners across the region are seeking packaging solutions that differentiate their products, improve performance, and advance sustainability without adding operational complexity,” said David Harf, President of Plastic Films Internacional SA. “By combining AeroFlexx’s packaging technology with PLAFILM’s regional expertise, we can help customers identify the right applications and accelerate commercialization.” The AeroFlexx technology is a lightweight flexible package designed to perform like a rigid bottle. Its patented airframe technology provides structure throughout use, while an integrated self-sealing valve enables controlled dispensing without a separate cap or pump. The format reduces packaging components, improves transportation efficiency, and provides brands with a highly customizable platform for retail and ecommerce applications. “Partnerships like this are essential in pushing industry innovation forward,” said Boris Gavric, Chief Operating Officer of AeroFlexx. “By combining our technology with PLAFILM’s regional reach, we can engage more customers, move qualified opportunities from evaluation to commercial launch, and establish a foundation for long-term regional deployment and scale.” The companies will initially concentrate on market development, project qualification, and customer conversion. As the commercial pipeline advances, AeroFlexx and PLAFILM may evaluate additional forms of regional collaboration that support scalable execution. About Plastic Films Internacional SA Plastic Films Internacional SA is a Flexible Packaging company with high experience in printing and converting in a large range of applications, products, and markets. They have more than 25 years of experience working with the most renowned brands in Colombia, Venezuela, Central America, and the Caribbean. Their greatest strengths are flexibility and high quality standards as an integrated packaging solution partner. They are committed to a more sustainable world and will keep working and investing to meet that goal in the future. To learn more, please visit www.plafilm.com . About AeroFlexx AeroFlexx is an integrated, end-to-end liquid packaging company revolutionizing sustainable solutions across a broad range of categories, including personal care, household products, baby care, pet care, food, and industrial applications. AeroFlexx’s proprietary technology transforms the packaging landscape by combining the advantages of flexible and rigid formats into a highly customizable offering that functions as both a primary package and a premium refill option. The result is a differentiated consumer experience, enhanced brand value, and industry-leading sustainability benefits. Headquartered in West Chester, Ohio, AeroFlexx is part of the Innventure ( NASDAQ:INV ) family of companies and provides packaging and manufacturing capabilities in North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. To learn more, visit https://aeroflexx.com or follow AeroFlexx on LinkedIn . info@aeroflexx.com

title: Best AI BDR Tools in 2026: 8 Platforms for Outbound Teams
summary: Compare the best AI BDR tools for outbound sales teams in 2026, including Trellus, Orum, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft, Apollo.io, ZoomInfo, and Clay.
body_text: AI BDR tools help outbound teams find accounts, prioritize prospects, fuel live conversations, automate follow-up, and coach reps. The right pick depends on your motion: phone-heavy calling, multichannel engagement, data-first prospecting, or custom AI personalization. This guide compares eight platforms relevant to AI-assisted outbound in 2026: Trellus, Orum, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft, Apollo.io, ZoomInfo Sales/Engage, and Clay. It’s written for sales leaders, frontline managers, RevOps, and founders deciding where AI should sit in the BDR workflow. If you’re weighing the broader landscape of AI for prospecting, see the companion hub on AI SDR software and this sibling roundup of best AI SDR tools . “AI BDR” and “AI SDR” overlap; what matters is your workflow and where AI should create leverage. What is an AI BDR tool? An AI BDR tool augments business development reps with intelligence and automation to find, contact, qualify, and convert outbound prospects. Common jobs supported: •Building prospect lists and enrichment •Researching accounts and contacts •Prioritizing who to contact next •Drafting or personalizing outreach and call notes •Powering parallel dialing and structured call flows •Prompting reps during live calls •Summarizing conversations and next steps •Automating follow-up tasks •Coaching reps based on behavior and outcomes •Enabling AI voice or agentic workflows For this article, “AI BDR tool” means software that supports outbound prospecting and pipeline creation—especially for calling, account research, sequencing, data, and rep coaching. How to evaluate AI BDR software Define the specific part of the BDR workflow you must improve before comparing vendors. Buy for workflow fit, not hype. Document your baseline (connects, qualified meetings, reply quality, ramp time, coaching capacity) so you can measure impact. Best AI BDR Tools in 2026: 8 Platforms for Outbound Teams — Table 1 Evaluation area What to assess Buyer questions to ask Core outbound motion Calling, email, sequencing, enrichment, coaching, autonomous outreach Where do we lose time: list building, dialing, personalization, follow-up, or coaching? Human vs. AI control Assistive AI vs. automation vs. fully autonomous outreach What should be human-in-the-loop vs. automated? Calling workflow Dialing speed, live prompts, notes, coaching, handoffs Does it improve conversation quality or just increase volume? Data quality and targeting Accuracy, coverage, freshness, signals How will we validate data for our ICP before rollout? Personalization AI-assisted research and relevant messaging Can it deliver useful context vs. generic fluff? CRM and workflow fit Sync, tasking, field mapping, reporting, RevOps controls What must sync, and who owns hygiene? Coaching and visibility Live guidance, review, scorecards, insights Can managers diagnose behavior, not just counts? Compliance and governance Consent, recording, AI disclosure, data handling What policies vary by region, channel, role? Time to value Setup, onboarding, enablement, change management Can we pilot in a contained segment first? Commercial fit Pricing, limits, seats, support, terms Which plan and integrations are required? The 8 best AI BDR tools to consider in 2026 These platforms serve different jobs (calling, engagement, data, workflow). Your ideal stack may combine an engagement system, a calling layer, a data source, and a coaching workflow—or a leaner all-in-one for smaller teams. Always confirm current capabilities and packaging with the vendor. teams that want AI-assisted calling, live rep support, and human-led workflows AI-assisted outbound across parallel dialing , real-time sales coaching , and AI voice agents for teams exploring confirm data providers, credit usage, integrations, governance 1. Trellus Trellus is designed for conversation-led outbound. It helps BDRs spend more time in live selling while receiving AI support before, during, and after calls. Publicly positioned capabilities include parallel dialing , real-time sales coaching , and AI voice agents . Best fits when your team: •Relies on calling as a primary channel •Wants more connects without lowering call quality •Prefers in-call guidance over only post-call review •Needs manager visibility into talk tracks and coaching moments •Is exploring AI voice for targeted workflows •Seeks a practical AI layer for rep execution, not just data or email What to verify: •Current plan packaging and pricing •Supported integrations and CRM field mapping •Usage limits and onboarding requirements •Internal policies for call recording, AI usage, and dialing rules by region •Availability and guardrails for AI voice workflows 2. Orum Orum is often shortlisted by teams aiming to increase live conversations via dialing. The core question is not just “Can reps dial faster?” but “Does it reliably create more qualified conversations while preserving data quality and compliance?” Evaluate: •Dialer modes and workflow options •CRM/engagement integrations and data sync behavior •AI assistance by plan •Dispositions, notes, analytics, and manager visibility •Regional dialing rules and compliance support •Admin setup and rep onboarding 3. Nooks Nooks appeals to teams that value collaborative calling, dialing rooms, and focused prospecting sessions. It can help standardize calling habits and surface coaching opportunities, which is useful for ramping reps and teams that want to institutionalize best practices. Evaluate: •Dialer and call workflow capabilities •AI coaching or in-call assistance •Manager views and rep performance insights •CRM and engagement integrations •Recording, transcription, and compliance controls •Setup effort, adoption requirements, usage limits, and pricing 4. Outreach Outreach is a sales engagement platform frequently chosen by mid-market and enterprise orgs needing sequences, governance, rep workflows, and reporting across teams. For BDRs, it can act as the engagement “OS” rather than a single-purpose tool. Evaluate: •AI-assisted messaging, prioritization, and workflow features •Sequencing depth and task orchestration •CRM integration quality and admin controls •Reporting and attribution workflows •Conversation intelligence or coaching options •Governance and permissions •Implementation timeline, enablement needs, and plan requirements for AI 5. title: Champion tracking: How to catch past buyers when they change jobs
summary: Why a champion's job change is the highest-converting outbound signal, how to track it, and the playbook to act before anyone else.
body_text: Champion tracking watches your past buyers and users for job changes, then alerts you the moment one lands at a new company. It is the highest-converting outbound signal there is, because a champion who already bought and liked your product arrives at a new employer with budget, authority, and a reason to bring you in. Artisan tracks champion job changes natively and runs the outreach the instant the signal fires. Why is a champion's job change the highest-converting signal? Because it removes the two things that make cold outbound hard. Normal prospecting has to build trust from zero and convince a stranger the category is worth buying. A champion who changes jobs has already done both. They ran your product at their last company, they know it works, and they carry that conviction into a new role that comes with fresh budget and often more authority than they had before. That is why these signals sit near the top of most outbound playbooks. You already have an advocate who now has a new problem you know how to solve. The message writes itself, reply rates clear cold benchmarks by a wide margin, and sales cycles compress because the hardest objection, "why should I trust this," is gone before you send. A single tracked champion moving into a buying role can be worth more than a hundred cold accounts. When should I reach out after a champion changes jobs? Inside the first 90 days, and sooner is better. A leader stepping into a new role spends that first quarter auditing what they inherited and deciding what to keep, cut, and add. That is the window when tools are chosen and stacks rebuilt, and a champion who loved your product is primed to bring it in, if you reach them before the slot fills with something else. Wait past the honeymoon and the read weakens. Budgets are committed, the new hire's priorities harden, and your warm advantage cools into just another vendor email. So of all the buying signals, champion tracking is the one where speed is least optional. Reaching a moved champion in week 2 rather than week 10 is often what separates a fast yes from a "we just signed with someone else." That urgency is exactly why the signal is worth automating, because a human tracking a contact list by hand will always be slower than a system that fires the moment a change is detected. The same timing logic runs through intent signals generally. How do I track when my champions change jobs? You need a maintained list of the people worth watching and a way to detect when their employer changes. Start by building the list: past buyers, power users, and internal advocates from closed-won and even closed-lost deals, pulled from your CRM. Then you need monitoring, because manually checking a few hundred contacts' profiles is not a real process. Tracking is only half the job, and activation is the half that converts. The wider market of intent data providers has the same split. What is the champion job-change playbook? Work both sides of the move. The first side is obvious: reach the champion at their new company with a warm, specific note that references your shared history without being heavy-handed, and offer to help them stand up what worked before. Because they already trust the product, keep it short and human, and let the relationship do the selling. The second side is the seat they left. When a champion moves, their old role is usually backfilled by someone new who has no loyalty to your product and may be evaluating alternatives. That is both a retention risk to defend and, viewed from the other direction, the same signal in reverse: a new decision-maker just landed in a role that touches your category. The complete playbook treats every champion move as two events, a warm opportunity at the destination and an open seat at the origin, and works them together.
